You are writing a concrete EXECUTION PLAN for a secondary-income business for Hooman (Adobe eng manager; $25-150K capital; ~10-20 hrs/wk alongside a day job; wants $5-30K/mo; already building CutLog).

IDEA: "Certification / licensing exam-prep course (mandated exam)"

The deep-research/validation stage produced these findings (JSON) — BUILD THE PLAN AROUND THE VALIDATED REALITY, not the original optimistic pitch:
{
  "idea": "Build an online exam-prep course for a legally-mandated certification exam (mid-size, weak-incumbent niche)",
  "slug": "exam_prep_course",
  "assumptions_checked": [
    {
      "claim": "Legally-mandated, non-optional, low-churn demand",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "FAA Part 107 is legally required to fly commercially; ~67,576 took the sUAS test in 2024 (84.2% pass), ~64,507 certs 2023, ~490K total remote pilots 2025. Mandated exams produce a steady annual inflow of new candidates. Caveat: demand is new-entrants-only (buy once), so revenue = annual new-cohort volume, not cumulative population. Source: FAA UAS testing statistics via drone-industry aggregators."
    },
    {
      "claim": "85%+ gross margin",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Gross margin at 85%+ is real (trivial digital COGS). But the pitch conflates gross with net: the dominant real cost is customer acquisition (ads on high-competition exam keywords, SEO/YouTube) plus content refresh. Net/owner margin is far below 85%. True but practically irrelevant to profit."
    },
    {
      "claim": "$5-25K/mo once ranked",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Arithmetically plausible (67K takers x few % x ~$200-300). But 'once ranked' is the whole game and is exactly what incumbents already own. This is the winner's outcome, not the median; median new course in a niche with an entrenched incumbent makes near zero. Platform earnings-distribution reports (Teachable/Podia) were unretrievable this session (404s), so median distribution is UNVERIFIED but industry-known survivorship bias applies (project LEARNING #2)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Near-passive after a 3-6mo build",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "Content is passive; the business is not. Ongoing non-delegable work: SEO cadence, YouTube, ad optimization, exam-change updates, student Q&A, publishing pass-rate proof, defending rank vs incumbents who outspend you. Pilot Institute runs a 29-person team. 'Passive' is the info-product marketing story, not the reality."
    },
    {
      "claim": "<$30K capital",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Bounded and accurate; course build + $1-2K test ads fits well under $30K. No inventory, no debt, no personal guarantee. The idea's strongest attribute; downside capped at lost time + a few $K."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Proof: Drone Launch Academy ~$50K/mo on FAA Part 107",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "$50K/mo is a real founder claim (David Young) but dates to ~2016-2018 early-mover window right after Part 107 launched (Aug 2016) with almost no competitors; also included drone-insurance revenue, not pure course sales. Third-party estimators (AllBiz $64K/yr, RocketReach $200K) do NOT corroborate sustained $50K/mo today. Primary interview unretrievable (404s). Most damning: the niche is now closed - Pilot Institute (145K+ students, ~$1M rev, 29 staff, refund guarantee) and Drone Pilot Ground School (85K+ trained, $299) dominate. Outlier + stale + unrepresentative."
    },
    {
      "claim": "A mid-size mandated exam with rising volume AND weak/dated incumbents exists (the key open question)",
      "status": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Every founder-adjacent candidate probed already had a strong entrenched specialist: insurance (Kaplan/ExamFX/AD Banker), EPA 608 (ESCO/Mainstream, low price), NABCEP (SEI/HeatSpring, small), ham radio (free HamStudy dominates), pilot (Sporty's/King/Gleim). No large + rising + weak-incumbent niche found. This is the make-or-break assumption and it is unsupported - matches project LEARNING 'always check for entrenched incumbents.'"
    }
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "Pilot Institute (FAA Part 107 + pilot): 145,647+ students, ~$1M revenue with 29-person team in 2024 (GetLatka), founded 2018, 99.9%-pass + full-refund marketing",
    "Drone Pilot Ground School / UAV Coach: 85,000+ pilots trained, $299 individual / $249 group, $750/team Test Prep Plus upsell",
    "Drone Launch Academy (the pitch's proof): early-mover ~$50K/mo claim from 2016-18, also sells drone insurance; current third-party rev estimates $64K-$200K/yr",
    "Insurance licensing: Kaplan, ExamFX, AD Banker - national, decades-entrenched",
    "EPA 608 (HVAC): ESCO Institute, Mainstream Engineering (epatest.com) - dominant, cheap, much prep quasi-free",
    "NABCEP (solar PV): Solar Energy International (SEI), HeatSpring - recognized specialists",
    "Pilot (private/instrument): Sporty's, King Schools, Gleim - heavyweight incumbents",
    "Ham radio: HamStudy (free), ARRL, Ham Radio Prep - strong free option caps pricing"
  ],
  "economics_verified": "Capital $10-30K (pitch correct, arguably conservative). Gross margin 85%+ TRUE but net margin gutted by ad/SEO CAC + content refresh (pitch misleadingly quotes gross as if it were owner profit). Revenue: median outcome $0-3K/mo, NOT $5-25K/mo; the $5-25K/mo is a top-decile 'if you win the ranking war' outcome (the changed number - pitch omits that 'once ranked' is the whole game). Time: 15-20 hrs/wk ONGOING (content/ads/SEO/refresh), NOT passive after build (the biggest changed claim). Ramp: 3-6mo build PLUS 12-24mo distribution grind to reach rank/revenue (pitch omits the distribution timeline). Downside: low, capped at build spend, no debt/PG - holds.",
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "confidence": "MEDIUM",
  "kill_risks": [
    "No weak-incumbent niche actually exists - the load-bearing assumption; every viable mandated exam is already owned by a focused specialist",
    "Distribution grind (SEO/YouTube/ads vs entrenched specialists, 12-24mo) is Hooman's single documented weakness per TRACKB_REPORT section 5 - this idea routes INTO it, not around it",
    "Survivorship bias in the proof: $50K/mo is one 2016 early-mover outlier, partly insurance not courses, in a now-closed niche; median outcome near-zero",
    "Generic founder-fit / no moat: 'any smart generalist can build it' means anyone can clone it; his AI/infra edge is irrelevant",
    "Exam-change risk: certifying body can revise the exam, forcing costly refresh and invalidating rank/reviews",
    "Free or employer-provided alternatives (ham radio, much EPA 608) cap willingness-to-pay in otherwise-plausible niches",
    "Opportunity cost: opens a SECOND 0-to-1 distribution front while CutLog is still in its own 0-to-1 grind - the exact trap the master report warns against"
  ],
  "best_niche_or_target": "No verified 'large + rising + weak-incumbent' niche exists - that assumption failed validation. Least-bad framing if pursued anyway: a narrow, genuinely technical mandated exam adjacent to his EE/RF/wireless/cloud skills where he can produce visibly better technical content than a generalist incumbent (e.g., a specific RF/wireless/networking operator certification), accepting a small $3-8K/mo ceiling and the distribution grind. But do NOT pick a niche until primary data (annual test-taker count from the certifying body + audit of top-3 incumbent quality/spend) proves a real gap - that validation IS the entire first bet. Explicitly avoid Part 107, insurance, pilot, PMP/CPA (all saturated).",
  "_idea": {
    "slug": "exam_prep_course",
    "name": "Certification / licensing exam-prep course (mandated exam)",
    "claims": "Legally-mandated demand; 85%+ margin; near-passive after a 3-6mo build; $5-25K/mo once ranked; <$30K capital. Proof cited: Drone Launch Academy ~$50K/mo on FAA Part 107. Key open question: WHICH mid-size mandated exam has rising volume AND weak/dated incumbents (not PMP/CPA which are saturated)?"
  }
}

Also read your own research doc at /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/exam_prep_course/01_research_validation.md for detail.

Write a concrete, realistic execution plan:
  - The specific target (exact niche/exam/tool/vertical/acquisition profile chosen in research).
  - First 90 days: week-by-week concrete actions, who does what, what gets validated when.
  - Months 4-12: path to the revenue target, hiring/delegation plan (this MUST stay part-time for Hooman).
  - Itemized budget within $25-150K; monthly burn; break-even point.
  - Revenue model + realistic ramp curve (subscribers/clients/deals over time).
  - Concrete go/no-go decision gates and the cheapest possible validation BEFORE committing real money.
  - How it coexists with CutLog for Hooman's limited hours (capital+delegation vs focus).

WRITE the plan to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/exam_prep_course/02_execution_plan.md (use Write). Return a ~200-word summary of the plan as your final text.

1	# Deep Research + Validation — Certification / Licensing Exam-Prep Course
2	
3	**Idea**: Build an online exam-prep course for a legally-mandated certification exam.
4	**Track-B rank**: #1 by raw score (8.6) in `TRACKB_REPORT.md`, but flagged #2 *for Hooman*
5	because founder-fit is generic.
6	**Date**: 2026-07-01. **Researcher**: Claude (Opus 4.8). **Method**: WebFetch against
7	DuckDuckGo/Bing/primary sources. Note: search engines heavily rate-limited (CAPTCHAs) during
8	this session; where a claim could not be independently sourced it is marked UNVERIFIED rather
9	than asserted.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 0. TL;DR verdict
14	
15	**CONDITIONAL → leaning PASS as a *primary* second stream. Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.**
16	
17	The *shape* is real: legally-mandated demand is genuine, gross margins on digital courses are
18	genuinely 85%+, and one real proof point (Drone Launch Academy) did reach ~$50K/mo. But three
19	things break the pitch as written:
20	
21	1. **The proof example is now a cautionary tale, not a template.** The exact niche used to
22	   sell this idea (FAA Part 107) is today one of the *most* saturated exam-prep niches in
23	   existence — Pilot Institute (145K+ students, ~$1M rev, 29 staff) and Drone Pilot Ground
24	   School (85K+ trained) own the SERPs and offer money-back-guarantee courses. A new entrant
25	   in 2026 cannot replicate 2016 Drone Launch.
26	2. **"Weak/dated incumbents" is largely a myth in the attractive niches.** Every mid-size
27	   mandated exam I probed already has an entrenched, well-capitalized specialist (Kaplan,
28	   ExamFX, AD Banker in insurance; ESCO/Mainstream in EPA 608; SEI/HeatSpring in NABCEP).
29	   This is the *exact* pattern this project's own LEARNINGS keep finding ("always check for
30	   entrenched incumbents before promoting"). The pitch's single load-bearing assumption —
31	   that such a niche is sitting there unclaimed — is the least-supported claim in it.
32	3. **"Near-passive after a 3–6mo build" is false.** Content is passive; *distribution is not.*
33	   The moat in this business is ranking (SEO/YouTube/ads) and maintaining pass-rate proof,
34	   which is ongoing work — and distribution to a fragmented buyer base is Hooman's documented
35	   single weakness (per `TRACKB_REPORT.md` §5). The build is the easy 20%.
36	
37	It is not a scam and it's capital-safe (<$30K, no debt/PG). But it is a **distribution grind
38	dressed up as a passive-income play**, competing head-on with focused incumbents, and it does
39	not use Hooman's unfair advantage. Given his real constraint is *time* (one serious venture at
40	a time, CutLog already in flight), this is a poor fit as a primary bet.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 1. Claim-by-claim validation
45	
46	### Claim A: "Legally-mandated demand (non-optional, low churn)"
47	**Status: VERIFIED (for the right exam).**
48	FAA Part 107 is legally required to fly a drone commercially; ~67,576 people took the sUAS
49	knowledge test in 2024 (84.2% pass), ~64,507 certs in 2023, ~490K total remote pilots as of
50	2025 (FAA testing-trend figures via multiple aggregators). Mandated exams do produce a steady,
51	recurring inflow of *new* candidates every year — genuinely different from optional courses.
52	Caveat: demand is for *new entrants only* (a given person buys once), so revenue is a function
53	of annual new-candidate volume, not cumulative population. A 60–70K/yr exam is a real but
54	finite pond, and you only capture a slice of one year's cohort at a time.
55	*Source: FAA UAS testing statistics as reported by drone-industry aggregators, 2024–2025.*
56	
57	### Claim B: "85%+ gross margin"
58	**Status: VERIFIED (gross), MISLEADING (net).**
59	Digital course COGS (hosting/video delivery) is trivial, so *gross* margin at 85%+ is real and
60	uncontroversial for info products. BUT the pitch quietly conflates gross margin with net/owner
61	economics. The dominant real cost is **customer acquisition** (paid ads on high-competition
62	exam keywords, SEO content production, YouTube) plus **content refresh** when the exam changes.
63	Once CAC is subtracted, net margin on a competitive exam-prep course is far below 85%. The 85%
64	figure is technically true and practically irrelevant to profit.
65	
66	### Claim C: "$5–25K/mo once ranked"
67	**Status: PARTIALLY-TRUE / survivorship-biased.**
68	Achievable arithmetically: 67K annual takers × capture a few % × ~$200–300 = mid-five figures
69	/mo is plausible IF you rank. The load-bearing phrase is **"once ranked."** Ranking is the
70	whole game and is precisely what incumbents already own. I could not find any platform-published
71	distribution of course-creator earnings this session (Teachable/Payhip report pages 404'd), but
72	the well-established industry reality — and this project's own LEARNING #2 — is that top-decile
73	outcomes get quoted as if typical. "$5–25K/mo" is the *winner's* outcome, not the median. The
74	median new exam-prep course in a niche with an entrenched incumbent makes near zero.
75	*Sources: FAA volumes above; Teachable/Podia earnings reports not retrievable this session
76	(UNVERIFIED distribution).*
77	
78	### Claim D: "Near-passive after a 3–6mo build"
79	**Status: FALSE (as stated).**
80	The *content* is passive after build; the *business* is not. Ongoing, non-delegable-at-first
81	work: SEO content cadence, YouTube, ad management/optimization, updating for exam changes,
82	answering student questions, maintaining/publishing pass-rate proof, and defending rank against
83	incumbents who out-spend you. Pilot Institute runs a 29-person team for a reason. "Passive" is
84	the marketing story of the info-product world; the reality is a content+distribution operation.
85	
86	### Claim E: "<$30K capital"
87	**Status: VERIFIED.**
88	Bounded and accurate. Course build (tools, video, question-bank authoring, a bit of design) +
89	$1–2K test ad spend fits well under $30K. This is genuinely the idea's strongest attribute:
90	low, capped, no inventory, no debt, no personal guarantee. Downside = lost time + a few $K.
91	
92	### Claim F (proof): "Drone Launch Academy ~$50K/mo on FAA Part 107"
93	**Status: PARTIALLY-TRUE but UNREPRESENTATIVE (outlier + stale + not pure-course).**
94	- The $50K/mo figure is a real founder claim (David Young), consistently repeated as "went
95	  from zero to ~$50K/mo within the first 24 months" — but it dates to ~2016–2018, i.e. the
96	  *early-mover* window right after Part 107 launched (Aug 2016) when there were almost no
97	  competitors. Bing/DDG aggregators (Achieve Success From Home, Online Course Igniter) repeat
98	  this; I could not retrieve the primary interview (404s), so the *exact* figure is
99	  ASSUMED-from-secondary-sources.
100	- Third-party revenue estimators show much smaller current figures ($64K–$200K/yr per AllBiz/
101	  RocketReach) — unreliable, but they do NOT corroborate a sustained $50K/mo today.
102	- Drone Launch also monetized **drone insurance** and other adjacent products, so "$50K/mo"
103	  is not cleanly attributable to course sales alone.
104	- Most important: **the niche it proves is now closed.** Pilot Institute (founded 2018, 145K+
105	  students, "$1M rev with 29-person team in 2024" per GetLatka, 99.9% pass claim + full-refund
106	  guarantee) and Drone Pilot Ground School / UAV Coach (85K+ trained, $299 course) now
107	  dominate. A 2026 entrant faces the incumbents *created by* the very opportunity the pitch
108	  cites. **The proof example actively argues against entering drone, and illustrates that any
109	  attractive exam niche gets colonized fast.**
110	
111	### Claim G (key open question): "a mid-size mandated exam with rising volume AND weak/dated incumbents exists"
112	**Status: UNVERIFIED / likely FALSE for the attractive niches.** See §2 — every candidate I
113	probed already had a strong specialist incumbent. This is the make-or-break assumption and it
114	is unsupported.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 2. Competitor / niche reconnaissance (the real question)
119	
120	The pitch lives or dies on finding a mid-size mandated exam with *weak* incumbents. I probed
121	the obvious founder-adjacent (technical/EE/trade) candidates. Finding: the good niches are
122	already owned; the "open" niches are open because they're too small or genuinely free.
123	
124	| Candidate mandated exam | Annual volume (approx) | Incumbents found | Verdict |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| **FAA Part 107 (drone)** | ~67K/yr takers | Pilot Institute (145K+ students, ~$1M rev, 29 staff, refund guarantee); Drone Pilot Ground School/UAV Coach (85K+ trained, $299) | SATURATED — the pitch's own example is now closed |
127	| **Insurance producer/adjuster license** | Large (state-by-state) | Kaplan, ExamFX, AD Banker — national, well-capitalized, decades-entrenched | SATURATED |
128	| **EPA 608 (HVAC refrigerant)** | Very high volume (huge tech base) | ESCO Institute, Mainstream Engineering (epatest.com) — dominant, cheap; much prep is quasi-free/employer-provided | LOW PRICE POINT + entrenched |
129	| **NABCEP (solar PV)** | Smaller/niche | SEI (Solar Energy International), HeatSpring — the recognized specialists | SMALL + entrenched |
130	| **Amateur radio (ham) license** | Meaningful volume | HamStudy (free), ARRL, Ham Radio Prep — a strong *free* option dominates | FREE-OPTION KILLS PRICING |
131	| **FAA private/instrument (pilot)** | Large | Sporty's, King Schools, Pilot Institute, Gleim — heavyweight incumbents | SATURATED |
132	
133	Named incumbent scale (verified this session):
134	- **Pilot Institute**: 145,647+ enrolled; "$1M revenue with a 29-person team in 2024"
135	  (GetLatka); founded 2018; 99.9%-pass + full-refund marketing. *Source: Bing aggregate +
136	  pilotinstitute.com claims.*
137	- **Drone Pilot Ground School (UAV Coach)**: 85,000+ pilots trained; $299 individual /
138	  $249 group; "Test Prep Plus" upsell $750/team. *Source: dronepilotgroundschool.com/pricing.*
139	- **Insurance**: Kaplan / ExamFX / AD Banker are the national standards (well-known; not
140	  independently price-scraped this session — treat scale as ASSUMED-strong).
141	
142	**Pattern confirmed** (matches this project's LEARNINGS "always check for entrenched
143	incumbents"): there is no free lunch. Either (a) the niche is big enough to be worth it and is
144	already owned by a focused specialist, or (b) it's "open" because it's tiny, low-priced, or has
145	a strong free competitor. The pitch's premise of a large, rising, weak-incumbent niche is the
146	unicorn, and I found no evidence one exists among the founder-adjacent options.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 3. Re-derived realistic economics (vs pitch)
151	
152	| Metric | Pitch | Realistic (this analysis) | What changed |
153	|---|---|---|---|
154	| Capital | <$30K | **$10–30K** | Confirmed — pitch is right, arguably conservative |
155	| Gross margin | 85%+ | **85%+ gross; but net margin gutted by CAC/ads/SEO labor** | Gross true, net misleading |
156	| Revenue | $5–25K/mo "once ranked" | **$0–3K/mo likely (median); $5–25K/mo only if you win the ranking war in a viable niche** | "Once ranked" is doing all the work; median outcome is near-zero |
157	| Time | Passive after 3–6mo | **15–20 hrs/wk *ongoing* (content, ads, SEO, refresh) — NOT passive** | The core claim that fails |
158	| Ramp | 3–6mo build | **3–6mo build + 12–24mo distribution grind to reach rank/revenue** | Missing the distribution timeline entirely |
159	| Downside | low | **Low (capped at build spend, no debt/PG) — this holds** | Confirmed |
160	
161	Net: capital and downside claims are solid; the income, passivity, and ramp claims are
162	optimistic-to-wrong because they omit the distribution war against incumbents.
163	
164	---
165	
166	## 4. Kill-risks
167	
168	1. **No weak-incumbent niche actually exists** (the load-bearing assumption). Every viable
169	   mandated exam is already owned. If you can't find the niche, there is no business.
170	2. **Distribution grind = Hooman's documented weakness.** Ranking a new course via

174	3. **Survivorship bias in the proof.** $50K/mo is one early-mover outlier from 2016, partly

176	4. **Generic founder-fit / no moat.** "Any smart generalist can build it" = anyone can clone
177	   it. No durable advantage; his AI/infra edge is irrelevant here.
178	5. **Exam-change risk.** The certifying body can revise the exam, forcing a costly content
179	   refresh and temporarily invalidating your rank/reviews.
180	6. **Free/employer-provided alternatives** (ham radio, much EPA 608) cap willingness-to-pay in
181	   several otherwise-plausible niches.
182	7. **Opportunity cost is the real killer.** It opens a *second* 0→1 distribution front while
183	   CutLog is still in its own 0→1 grind — the precise trap the master report warns against.
184	
185	---
186	
187	## 5. Best-fit niche (if pursued anyway)

189	There is no verified "large + rising + weak-incumbent" niche. The *least-bad* framing, if

192	e.g. a specific RF/wireless/networking or emerging-tech operator certification — accepting it

202	**CONDITIONAL, leaning PASS as a primary second stream. Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.**
203

# Execution Plan — Certification / Licensing Exam-Prep Course (Mandated Exam)

**For**: Hooman Shariati (Adobe eng manager; ~10–20 hrs/wk; $25–150K capital available; target $5–30K/mo; already building CutLog).
**Slug**: `exam_prep_course`. **Date**: 2026-07-01. **Author**: Claude (Opus 4.8).
**Verdict feeding this plan**: PASS, MEDIUM confidence — but *conditional*. See `01_research_validation.md`.

---

## 0. Read this first — what this plan is NOT

The original pitch ("build a course on a mandated exam, 85% margin, near-passive after 3–6 months, $5–25K/mo")
is **rewritten here around the validated reality**:

- **It is a DISTRIBUTION business, not a passive-income business.** Content build is the easy 20%. Ranking (SEO/YouTube/ads) against focused incumbents is the whole game and is ongoing 15–20 hrs/wk work.
- **The headline number is a top-decile outcome, not the median.** Median new course in an owned niche makes ~$0–3K/mo. $5–25K/mo is "if you win the ranking war."
- **The load-bearing assumption is UNVERIFIED.** No "large + rising + weak-incumbent" niche was found in research. Every attractive mandated exam (Part 107, insurance, EPA 608, NABCEP, ham, pilot) is already owned by an entrenched specialist. **Finding a real gap IS the first bet.**
- **This attacks Hooman's one documented weakness** (fragmented-buyer distribution grind) while CutLog is still in its own 0→1 grind.

**Therefore this plan is front-loaded with a cheap KILL GATE.** ~$0–500 and ~15–20 hours of Hooman's time are spent proving a niche exists *before* any course is built. If Gate 0 fails, STOP. Do not build.

---

## 1. The specific target

Research found **no verified viable niche**. The plan does not pretend otherwise. Instead:

**Phase 0 selects the target via primary data.** The target is defined by a filter, not a guess:

> A mandated/legally-required certification exam with **≥30–50K new candidates/year** (from the certifying body's own published test-taker stats — not aggregators), a **defensible $150+ price point**, and **top-3 incumbents that are demonstrably weak** (dead/dated sites, no recent exam-update, poor reviews, no refund guarantee, no active YouTube/SEO presence).

**Least-bad bias if a tie:** a **narrow, genuinely technical exam adjacent to Hooman's EE/RF/wireless/cloud skills** — where he can produce *visibly better technical content* than a generalist incumbent, giving a thin content moat a generalist can't clone as fast. Candidate hunting-ground exams to *probe* (NOT pre-committed; must pass Gate 0):
- RF/wireless operator or radio-frequency safety certs
- Specific networking/cloud/security operator certs that are *employer-mandated* and where incumbents are stale
- Emerging-tech operator licenses (new enough that incumbents haven't colonized, old enough to have volume)

**Explicitly BANNED targets** (saturated — auto-reject): FAA Part 107 / drone, insurance producer/adjuster, EPA 608, NABCEP, FAA pilot (private/instrument), PMP, CPA, ham radio (free HamStudy caps price).

---

## 2. Cheapest-possible validation BEFORE money — Gate 0 (Weeks 1–3)

This is the entire first bet. **Cost: ~$0–500. Time: ~15–20 hrs total.** No course built yet.

**Deliverable: a one-page "Niche Dossier" scoring 8–12 candidate exams** on four hard filters. Each filter is pass/fail; a niche must pass all four.

| Filter | How to check (cheap) | Pass bar |
|---|---|---|
| **Volume** | Certifying body's *own* published test-taker/pass stats (FOIA-style pages, annual reports). NOT third-party estimators. | ≥30K new candidates/yr |
| **Price** | What do existing courses charge? Is there a strong FREE option? | Sustainable ≥$150; no dominant free competitor |
| **Incumbent weakness** | Manually audit top-3 Google/YouTube results: last content update, review quality, refund guarantee, ad presence (check if they bid on keywords via a $50 Google Ads test or SpyFu free tier) | ≥2 of top-3 are dated/absent/weak |
| **Founder edge** | Can Hooman produce *better technical* content than incumbents? | Yes for technical exams; No = deprioritize |

**Gate 0 decision:**
- **≥1 niche passes all four filters → GO to Phase 1** with that niche.
- **Zero niches pass → HARD STOP.** Kill the idea. Reallocate hours to CutLog. This is the expected outcome per research and is a *win* — you spent <$500 and ~20 hrs to avoid a 12–24 month distribution grind that loses to incumbents.

> **Do NOT rationalize a marginal niche through Gate 0.** The research already found that borderline niches lose. If nothing clears cleanly, stop.

---

## 3. First 90 days — week by week

### Phase 0 — Niche validation (Weeks 1–3) — Hooman solo, ~5–7 hrs/wk

| Week | Actions | Owner | Validated by end of week |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build candidate list (8–12 mandated exams). Pull certifying-body volume stats for each. Kill any <30K/yr. | Hooman | Volume filter applied; list cut to ~4–6 |
| 2 | For survivors: audit top-3 incumbents (site freshness, reviews, refund guarantee, ad spend via SpyFu free / $50 Ads keyword test). Note price points + free-option risk. | Hooman (can delegate the manual audit to a VA, ~$100) | Incumbent-weakness + price filters applied |
| 3 | Score all four filters into the Niche Dossier. **GATE 0 decision.** If GO, run a $200–300 Google Ads "smoke test": a fake landing page ("[Exam] Prep Course — join waitlist") to measure real click intent + CPC on the target keywords. | Hooman | CPC + click-through-rate data; realistic CAC estimate |

**Gate 0 exit criteria (all must hold):** niche passes 4 filters AND smoke-test CPC implies CAC < ~30% of price (e.g. price $250 → CAC under ~$75). If CPC is so high that CAC eats the margin, STOP — the ad channel is owned.

### Phase 1 — Minimum sellable course (Weeks 4–9) — Hooman + contractors

Only entered if Gate 0 = GO.

| Week | Actions | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Buy the exam's official study guide + take the real exam yourself (be a subject expert). Draft course outline mapped 1:1 to exam objectives. | Hooman |
| 5–6 | Author the **question bank** (150–300 practice questions w/ explanations) — this is the actual product/moat, not the videos. Hooman writes the technical core; a contractor formats/QAs. | Hooman + contractor ($1–2K) |
| 7 | Record core video lessons (screen + voice, no fancy production). Set up on Teachable/Podia/Thinkific ($40–120/mo). | Hooman + editor ($1–2K) |
| 8 | Build the sales landing page + set up pass-rate tracking (survey buyers post-exam). Simple, one page, refund guarantee. | Hooman + VA |
| 9 | **Soft launch**: run the same $200–300 ad set to the *real* course. Target: first 5–10 paying buyers. | Hooman |

### Phase 2 — First revenue + rank foundation (Weeks 10–13)

| Week | Actions | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Collect first buyer feedback + pass results. Fix the top-3 complaints. | Hooman |
| 11–12 | Start SEO/YouTube content engine: 1 pillar article + 1 YouTube walkthrough/wk. This is the long game (ranking). Delegate writing to a niche-literate contractor; Hooman does technical QA. | Contractor ($1–1.5K/mo) + Hooman QA |
| 13 | **GATE 1 decision** (see §6). | Hooman |

**End-of-90-day target:** niche validated, sellable course live, **10–25 paying customers** (~$2–6K cumulative revenue), CAC measured against real payment data, SEO/YouTube engine running.

---

## 4. Months 4–12 — path to revenue + delegation (MUST stay part-time)

The core constraint: **Hooman must not become the operator.** His weekly role caps at ~5 hrs (technical content QA + exam-change monitoring + strategic decisions). Everything else is delegated.

**Delegation stack (this is how it stays part-time):**
- **Content contractor / niche writer** (~$1–2K/mo): SEO articles + YouTube scripts + community answers.
- **Video editor** (per-project, ~$500–1K/mo): repurpose lessons into YouTube/shorts.
- **Media buyer / VA** (~$500–1.5K/mo, ramp when CAC is proven positive): manage paid ads.
- Hooman: technical accuracy, exam-change updates (non-delegable), P&L decisions.

**Revenue path (realistic, incumbent-adjusted):**

| Month | New buyers/mo | Price | MRR-equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 5–10 | $200–300 | $1–3K | Paid-ads-driven, CAC-heavy, near break-even |
| 6 | 15–30 | $200–300 | $3–8K | SEO/YouTube starting to contribute organic buyers (lower CAC) |
| 9 | 25–50 | $200–300 | $6–15K | Rank climbing IF niche gap was real; otherwise plateau at ~$3K |
| 12 | 40–80 | $200–300 | $10–24K | **Top-decile / "won the ranking war" outcome.** Median realistic = $3–8K/mo. |

> Model both. **Base case: $3–8K/mo by month 12** (meets the low end of the target with a small ceiling). **Upside: $10–24K/mo** only if the niche gap was genuinely underserved AND organic rank compounds. Do not budget on upside.

**Buy-once dynamics:** revenue = annual new-cohort volume × capture rate × price. There is no recurring subscription base — you must re-win each year's cohort. Add upsells (team licenses, refresher/recert bundles, adjacent cert) to raise LTV.

---

## 5. Budget (within $25–150K), monthly burn, break-even

This is a **deliberately cheap** idea — its best attribute. Do NOT spend to the cap; the cap is headroom, not a target.

**One-time (Phase 0–1, ~first 90 days): ~$5–9K**
| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Gate 0 validation (VA audit + smoke-test ads) | $300–800 |
| Exam fee + study materials (become the expert) | $200–1,000 |
| Question-bank authoring contractor | $1,000–2,000 |
| Video editing (initial lessons) | $1,000–2,000 |
| Landing page / design / course platform setup | $500–1,500 |
| Initial soft-launch ad spend | $500–1,000 |
| **Total one-time** | **~$5–9K** |

**Ongoing monthly burn (Months 4–12): ~$3–6K/mo**
| Item | Monthly |
|---|---|
| Content contractor (SEO/YouTube) | $1,000–2,000 |
| Video editor | $500–1,000 |
| Paid ads (scale only with positive CAC) | $1,000–2,500 |
| Course platform + tools | $100–300 |
| **Total burn** | **~$3–6K/mo** |

**Total 12-month capital exposure: ~$40–70K** — comfortably inside $25–150K, with the caveat that **spend ramps only behind proof** (don't hit $6K/mo burn until revenue justifies it).

**Break-even:** at $3–6K/mo burn and ~$250 price, break-even is **~15–25 new buyers/mo**. Base case reaches this around **month 6–9**. If not break-even by month 9, that is a NO-GO signal (Gate 2).

---

## 6. Go/No-Go decision gates

| Gate | When | GO if | NO-GO → action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gate 0** (the real bet) | End Week 3 | ≥1 niche passes all 4 filters AND smoke-test CAC < 30% of price | **KILL the idea.** Spent <$500. Return hours to CutLog. |
| **Gate 1** | End Week 13 | 10–25 paying buyers AND blended CAC < 40% of price AND ≥1 organic signal (a ranking article gaining impressions) | Pause paid spend; try 4 more weeks of organic only. If still flat, kill. |
| **Gate 2** | Month 9 | ≥ break-even (15–25 buyers/mo) AND organic buyers growing | Wind down. Keep course as-is passively; stop all spend/contractors. Cut losses (<$40K). |
| **Gate 3** | Month 12 | ≥$5K/mo net AND trend up | Continue + consider a second adjacent cert. Below $5K → keep passive or sell the asset. |

**Cheapest validation principle:** every gate is designed so the *maximum* loss if you're wrong is small (Gate 0 <$500; Gate 1 <$10K; Gate 2 <$40K). No debt, no personal guarantee, no inventory.

---

## 7. How it coexists with CutLog (Hooman's scarce hours)

**The honest recommendation:** CutLog is the priority. This idea should only proceed as a **capital-and-delegation play, never a focus play.** The research is explicit that opening a second 0→1 *distribution* front while CutLog is still in its own 0→1 grind is the trap the master report warns against.

**Rules for coexistence:**
1. **Gate 0 first, and it's cheap enough to run without hurting CutLog** (~15–20 hrs over 3 weeks, spread thin). If Gate 0 fails — the likely outcome — you've lost almost nothing and CutLog keeps 100% of your focus.
2. **If Gate 0 passes, run this as a delegated operation, not a build.** Hooman's cap is ~5 hrs/wk (technical QA + exam monitoring + decisions). The distribution grind is *bought*, not personally executed — that is exactly why the budget carries contractors from month 3.
3. **CutLog always wins a time conflict.** If both need Hooman in the same week, exam-prep waits. Structure contractors so the exam business survives Hooman being absent for 2–3 weeks.
4. **Sequence, don't parallelize the hard part.** Do not start the exam-prep SEO grind until CutLog is either self-sustaining or clearly stalled. Two simultaneous distribution grinds guarantees both starve.
5. **Kill-readiness.** Because the moat is thin and founder-fit generic, treat this as a disposable experiment. Be willing to shut it at any gate without sunk-cost attachment.

---

## 8. Bottom line

- **Most likely path: Gate 0 fails, you kill the idea for <$500, and that is the correct, valuable outcome.**
- If Gate 0 passes with a genuine technical-adjacent niche, run it **delegated and part-time**, budget ~$40–70K over 12 months, aim for a realistic **$3–8K/mo** base case (upside $10–24K only if you win the rank war), break-even ~month 6–9.
- Never let it consume the building hours CutLog needs. This is a hedge funded by capital and contractors — not a second focus.
